correctness.rationale: The published equations (3.3) and (3.6) give the coefficients in the frozen statement, including right-end factor 2λ/(1+λ) under the homogeneous Neumann condition. At t_0=0 the diagonal coefficient is b_0=[1−λ+(M−m)Δt]/(1+λ), and b_n≥b_0 when the exponent is nonnegative. The left and right forward coefficients are nonnegative. If b_0,c≥0, induction through nodes and time steps preserves the closed cone, also at equality. If b_0<0, choose zero boundary and the first interior basis vector; if c<0, choose zero boundary and the second interior basis vector. The first output component isolates the respective offending coefficient, so no conclusion from a signed coefficient hidden by later sweep entries is required. Rearrangement gives exactly the two inequalities. Substituting the printed numerical values directly into the printed stencil gives λ=9, b_0=−79941/100000 and the time ceiling 100/89941. With the given nonconstant input h_1=25+exp(0.01)<27 and C_1^0=100,C_2^0=0, the upper bounds on the first interior output are −55.5735, −55.1685 and −54.7635 for the three velocities. The sign is independent of the nutrient/light exponent at t_0. Independent `python3 /workspace/checks/frozen_replay.py 5` passed exact sweeps of the cone generators on a 3×3 parameter grid that includes both equality boundaries, as well as the three exact witness bounds. The frozen claim is about the printed formula and direct numerical inputs, not the physical rescaling or what the authors' implementation and constant-25 initial condition do.
residual_risks: The primary paper reports normalized-looking mesh numbers alongside physical units in meters, seconds and days and gives inconsistent right-end locations. No internally consistent conversion to an implemented or physically scaled case was verified; λ=9 and the three witness bounds are for the raw printed numbers only.

The frozen proof assumes a fixed nonnegative exponent, while the source permits a Monod field μ(x,t). For sign purposes nonnegative field values still give b_(i,n)≥b_0 and the same t_0 coefficient, but no coupled nutrient evolution or certification of an implementation is claimed. 'Zero flux' here denotes the printed homogeneous Neumann condition, not zero total advective-plus-diffusive flux.

value.rationale: The general coefficient test alone is elementary. The useful result is the complete target-specific boundary with an explicit severe negative first-step value at each printed velocity under the article's own left boundary input. It separates universal numerical admissibility from stability and provides concrete guidance on when the printed update can guarantee meaningful nonnegative concentrations. The raw-numeric example exposes a reproducibility problem for any user who plugs the supplied grid numbers into the formula; it does not claim that the physically converted or plotted run is negative.
residual_risks: Physical unit reconciliation and the article's actual implementation remain outside the validated claim.
